name: OK-02
label: Safe R

key_factors: District partisan lean of roughly R+28, among the most Republican seats in the country
Incumbent Josh Brecheen has a massive financial edge, raising about $245,000 to under $8,000 for Democrat Brandon Wade
Prediction markets price Republican odds near 98%
No public polling and no expert raters flag the race as competitive
model.rationale: The district's R+28 fundamentals, Brecheen's incumbency, and his overwhelming fundraising advantage over a challenger with about $1,400 on hand leave virtually no path for Democrats, and markets price Republican odds near 98%. The expected margin sits around 21 points Republican, with only the national climate pulling it modestly toward the center.
model.watch: Only a major scandal or a double-digit national wave shifting the environment could put this seat in doubt.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Oklahoma's 2nd District is one of the most Republican-leaning seats in the country, with a partisan lean of roughly R+28. Incumbent Josh Brecheen, first elected in 2022, is seeking re-election after easily securing renomination. No general-election polling is available, and no expert raters list the race as competitive.

The financial picture is lopsided: Brecheen has raised about $245,000 while Democratic nominee Brandon Wade has raised under $8,000 and reported roughly $1,400 on hand. Prediction markets give Brecheen about a 98% chance of winning. The expected margin is around 21 points Republican, with the district's fundamentals only partially offset by a more favorable national climate for Democrats. An independent candidate is also on the ballot but shows no measurable support. The race is rated Safe Republican.
